version.value: Original version for flute, oboe, clarinet in A, horn in F and bassoon. The Menuet, the Trio, the written-out return of the Menuet and the Coda are present.
version.note: The structure of the track (a Menuet, a Trio in F major, a return of the Menuet and a Coda) was compared with the printed bars of the Carl Nielsen Edition; no published list of the side was consulted. The label reads “2 Sats: Menuet”. Which score edition the players used is not stated.

value.name: Det Kgl. Kapels Blæserkvintet (Wind Quintet of the Royal Orchestra, Copenhagen)

performers.note: The labels read “Det Kgl. Kapels Blæserkvintet. Gilbert Jespersen—Fløjte, Felumb—Oboe, Oxenvad—Klarinet, Kn. Lassen—Fagot & Hans Sørensen—Horn”. The Kelly files give the same five names, with Holger Gilbert-Jespersen in full, for the wind quintet of the Royal Orchestra, Copenhagen. The item description calls the ensemble the Wind Quintet of the Royal Danish Opera and says Gilbert-Jespersen joined in 1929; the Catalogue of Carl Nielsen’s Works lists him as the flautist at the Berlin performance of 29 March 1923, and Paul Hagemann as flautist at the first public performance on 9 October 1922.

date.note: The Kelly files list matrix 2CS 295 with four takes: takes 1 to 3 are dated January 1936 without a day, and take 4, the issued take, is dated 5 May 1936. The item description gives 24 January 1936 for the set as a whole and lists this side as 2CS 295-4. The rest of the quintet was recorded on 24 and 25 January 1936.

place.note: The item description places the quintet sessions in Copenhagen, and the Kelly files give “Royal Orchestra, Copenhagen” as the ensemble. The place field in the Kelly files reads “Someplace, Scandanavia”, a placeholder, and no place is stated for the May take specifically. The studio or hall is not stated.

label.value: His Master’s Voice (The Gramophone Company, Ltd.), 12-inch records in the Scandinavian red-label D.B. series, pressed in England
label.note: The label scan reads “His Master’s Voice”, “Made in England” and “The Gramophone Co. Ltd.”, in Danish, with “Quintett” and the speed, 78. The item description calls DB 5200–5203 the first issue in the 12-inch Scandinavian Red Label series.

catalogue.value: HMV D.B. 5201 (side A), “2 Sats: Menuet”; the set is D.B. 5200–5203, 12-inch, 78 rpm
catalogue.note: Read from the label scan of D.B. 5201 A, which also carries a hand-marked side number 3. The Musical Quarterly of April 1937 lists the set as DB 5200–3, and The New Records of August 1937 as four 12-inch discs, DB5200 to DB5203.

matrixTakeSides.note: The label prints the matrix number 2CS 295 without a take; take 4 comes from the item description and agrees with the issued take in the Kelly files.

credits.value: Internet Archive collection The Shellackophile’s Vintage Recordings; the person who made the transfer is not named in the item
credits.note: The item belongs to the collection described as recordings of classical music from the 78-rpm era. Photographs of the labels are included in the item; their photographer is not named.

date.value: Not stated; the item was made public on 17 March 2022
date.note: The public date of the item and the modification time of the uploaded FLAC file are the same day, which is an upload date and not a transfer date.

processing.value: One disc side of 4 min 28 s as one track. Equalisation, noise reduction and speed correction are not described.
processing.note: The movement is a single side, and the surface noise of the track is steady, with no join.

digital.format: Internet Archive derivative VBR MP3 from an uploaded FLAC

composition.value: Public domain. Nielsen died on 3 October 1931, so the work has been out of copyright in the European Union (life plus 70 years) since the end of 2001. The first edition was published by Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, in 1923, which makes it public domain in the United States as well.
composition.note: The dates are documented; the legal conclusion is ours. The Carl Nielsen Edition of 2003, used here only for bar numbers and the preface, is a separate publication under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 3.0 licence, and none of its text or music is reproduced.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
recording.note: The set was listed as Danish Gramophone DB 5200–3 in The Musical Quarterly of April 1937 and reviewed as four 12-inch discs in The New Records of August 1937, so it was published by then. The uploader’s date of 1936 is not an independent source. The United States status of a Danish recording published in 1936 or 1937 is not established.
